shower.thought: We spend years learning to read other people's minds, then call it a skill instead of admitting we're all just guessing.
The people who hurt you the most are usually the ones who showed you they could care about you first.
You've probably had the same conversation with different people so many times that you've forgotten who you originally stole it from.
Time moves slower when you're waiting for something and faster when you're trying to hold onto it, which means your perception of time is just measuring how much you want something to stay.
Most of your opinions aren't actually yours—they're just the first version you heard presented confidently.
You can't remember most of what you've learned, but you also can't do most of what you do without it.
The things that make you feel alive are often the things that prove how fragile your life actually is.
You're constantly being shaped by people who have no idea they're shaping you.
Boredom might just be your brain refusing to pretend something matters when it doesn't.
We treat our bodies like we're going to trade them in for a better model someday.
The older you get, the faster time moves, which means life accelerates just as you're finally starting to understand what you're doing.
Every person you'll never meet made decisions today that will somehow affect your future.
You can't actually prove that other people experience color the way you do, so you've been trusting strangers about reality your entire life.
The parts of yourself you hate the most are usually the parts that keep you safe.
Comfort is just a prison you decorated yourself.
You spend the first part of your life learning how to be yourself and the rest of your life trying to hide it.
The only reason you're not paranoid about all the things that could go wrong is because statistically most of them won't, but that's not the same as it being safe.
People confuse honesty with wisdom all the time—a fool can tell the truth, it just feels true because they're saying it.
Most disagreements end not because someone was proven wrong, but because they got tired of explaining themselves.
Your sense of humor is just a map of the things you've decided aren't worth taking seriously anymore.

motivational.thought: The man who moves a mountain begins by carrying away small stones. — Confucius
Comparison is the thief of joy. — Theodore Roosevelt
Your limitation—it's only your lack of vision. — Muhammad Ali
The cave you fear to enter holds the treasure you seek. — Joseph Campbell
Don't watch the clock; do what it does. Keep going. — Sam Levenson
Discipline is choosing between what you want now and what you want most. — Unknown
The only way out is through. — Robert Frost
You are not a drop in the ocean. You are the entire ocean in a drop. — Rumi
Most of life's failures are people who did not realize how close they were to success when they gave up. — Thomas Edison
Suffering ceases to be suffering at the moment it finds a meaning. — Viktor Frankl
The best time to plant a tree was 20 years ago. The second best time is now. — Ancient Proverb
Excellence is not a destination; it's a habit. — Aristotle
Your scars are evidence that you fought and survived. — Unknown
We cannot direct the wind, but we can adjust the sails. — Dolly Parton
The obstacle is the way. — Marcus Aurelius
What lies behind us and what lies before us are tiny matters compared to what lies within us. — Ralph Waldo Emerson
Every master was once a disaster. — T. Harv Eker
Do the work, especially when you don't feel like it. That's where the real growth lives. — Unknown
Peace comes from within. Do not seek it without. — Buddha
The person you'll become is determined by the books you read and the people you surround yourself with. — Will Smith

darkjoke.thought:
I told my date I was really into helping people.
She said that's sweet. I said, "I know—I'm a therapist," and immediately billed her for emotional labor.

My dad said he wanted to die doing what he loved.
Turns out that was disappointing everyone.

I'm reading a book about anti-gravity.
It's impossible to put down, which is ironic because my motivation is.

My friend said he was going to start journaling to process his emotions.
I said, "Good idea." He said, "Why?" I said, "So there's at least one record of you having them."

I asked my boss if I'd ever make partner.
He said, "Only if you keep working like you're replaceable."
I said, "I thought that was motivating." He said, "It was supposed to be."

My therapist asked if I ever felt like giving up.
I said, "Every day." She said, "That's good—means you're trying."

I told my friend he should see a therapist about his anxiety.
He asked why I kept recommending that. I said, "Because they need the business too."

My ex-girlfriend said she needed space.
I gave her the whole house and some legal distance.

I asked my doctor if there was anything I could do to live longer.
He said, "Stop coming to these appointments and worrying about it."

I'm terrible at keeping secrets.
My wife knows because I told my therapist, who probably told her patients, who definitely told their husbands.

My friend said he was going to change his life.
I said, "Good luck." He said, "Why?" I said, "Because you have a track record of finishing things you start, and that's never gone well."

I told my boss I was feeling burnt out.
He said, "Have you tried taking time off?" I said, "I have two weeks vacation." He said, "I meant permanently."

My parents asked why I wasn't married yet.
I said, "I'm still looking for someone who makes me as happy as being alone does."
They got really quiet.

I went to a motivational speaker who kept saying "You can do anything you set your mind to."
I set my mind to leaving early, and he was right.

My friend said he was going to start living his best life.
I said, "Finally." He said, "Why finally?" I said, "Because your current life is unwatchable."

My therapist asked what I wanted to work on this session.
I said, "Can we talk about my self-esteem?" She said, "Sure, but we should probably start with realistic goals first."

I told my mom I was depressed.
She said, "You should go outside more." I said, "Outside is where all the people are."

My coworker said she was on a new diet.
I asked how it was going. She said, "Great—I've lost ten pounds and my will to live."

I asked my friend why he never calls anymore.
He said, "I'm trying to be present in the moment." I said, "You're literally on your phone right now." He said, "Yeah, but not with you."

My dentist said I need to floss more.
I said, "I'll try." He said, "No, you won't." I said, "How did you know?" He said, "You said that six months ago. You haven't changed. You won't change."
